name: Omnicom Group Inc.
moat_justification: Moderate, scale-based moat, not structural: the IPG combination made Omnicom the world's largest holdco and #1 in global media billings ($75.6B, 31% share), with the Omni data/AI platform and Big Three pitch dynamics (91% of major H1 2026 pitches) rewarding scale. Against that, it is a people business with low client switching costs and regular account reviews, Publicis is out-executing on the same data/AI playbook ($2.2B net new business in Q3 2026 while Omnicom's H1 was negative), AI/platforms threaten disintermediation, and the $1.5B synergy target is promised, not delivered. CAP 8.5 years.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 13.12 vs 3-yr median 7.56 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 4.7x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: World's largest ad holdco post-IPG, moat 5/10 — clears 15% on the matched TTM base (15.8% weighted, IV $86.11 vs $80.72) but with almost no margin of safety, net debt 4.7x normalized OE, and a C-to-B method range; a low B, not a bargain.
moat_for: World's largest holdco post-IPG; Omnicom Media #1 globally with $75.6B billings (31% share) — media-buying leverage
Omni data/AI platform with Adobe, Google Cloud and Microsoft partnerships; Big Three won 91% of major H1 2026 pitches
Diversified connected capabilities and blue-chip roster; Q2 2026 core organic growth +6.1% with margin expansion
Asset-light: capex $181.5M TTM vs OCF $3,171.8M; SBC a modest $107.1M TTM
moat_against: People business — talent walks; post-merger network retirements and layoffs are a retention risk
Low switching costs — accounts reviewed and moved regularly; Publicis took $2.2B net new business in Q3 2026, Omnicom H1 net new business negative
AI/agentic disintermediation, client in-housing, and Google/Meta selling directly
Integration complexity — client conflicts, planned dispositions, $1.5B synergy target not yet delivered
Cyclical ad-spend exposure and principal-media transparency pressure
